name: minisat
why: A compact SAT solver that opens the door to constraint solving, though it is a classic and fairly standard tool.

brief.what_it_is: MiniSat is a small, open-source SAT solver: it takes a Boolean satisfiability problem, usually a CNF file passed on the command line, and reports whether it is satisfiable, with a model if so. The GitHub README covers only building and installing, plus one example run of the minisat binary on a CNF file. The minisat.se page describes it as a minimalistic, open-source SAT solver, and says it also supports incremental SAT and adding non-clausal constraints. Installed executables are minisat and minisat_core.
brief.why_it_exists: The minisat.se page says it was developed to help researchers and developers alike get started on SAT, and it is meant to be easy to modify and integrate as a backend for other tools.
brief.how_it_works: The source tree is split into mtl/ (Mini Template Library), utils/ (I/O, parsing, CPU-time helpers), core/ (a core version of the solver) and simp/ (an extended solver with simplification). The README does not explain the solving algorithm itself. The Examples section says the default run can be made to use the same heuristics as version 2.0 by passing flags.

commands_seen.context: Configures the build with a GNU-style install prefix; the README says this is the simplest approach and that configuration is stored in config.mk.
Compiles and installs MiniSat into the configured prefix.
Example run of the solver on a CNF file, using the same heuristics as version 2.0 according to the README.

brief.install_notes: Install with make config prefix=$PREFIX followed by make install, per the README. Configuration is saved to config.mk; delete it or run make distclean to reset. Recompiling does not need the config step. The README has no mention of hardware, accounts, or runtimes. Homebrew installs it as the package minisat, so the brew route should be used first.
brief.standout: It is famous for being small and readable while winning industrial categories at the SAT 2005 competition, which makes it a classic teaching and integration base. The minisat.se page highlights incremental use and a way to add non-clausal constraints.
brief.status: Unknown from what I could fetch. The GitHub README has no release or commit dates and several TODO placeholders. The minisat.se news list mentions a 2.2.0 release and points to the GitHub repo for the 2.2 source, but the page shows no date for the newest item.
brief.caveats: The GitHub README has unfinished sections marked TODO: compile-flag and mode configuration, separate build modes, and an install section. The README's build instructions are the only install guidance I found. The brew caveats field is empty. The fetched README did not describe the project's purpose; that came from the separate minisat.se page.

judge.reason: MiniSat is a compact, influential SAT solver whose readable implementation makes Boolean constraint solving tangible and worth exploring.

entry.title: MiniSat
entry.tldr: A small, readable SAT solver that decides whether a Boolean formula can be satisfied, and a classic door into constraint solving.
entry.deeper_look:
MiniSat takes a Boolean satisfiability problem, usually a CNF file named on the command line, and reports whether some assignment of true and false makes the whole formula true. If one exists, it prints a model.

It was written to help researchers and developers get started on SAT. The project page calls it "a minimalistic, open-source SAT solver" and says it is meant to be easy to modify and to serve as a backend for other tools. It also supports incremental SAT and a way to add non-clausal constraints. It is famous for winning all the industrial categories at the SAT 2005 competition while staying small and well documented.

The idea underneath is that a surprising number of hard problems can be written as one giant true-or-false formula and handed to a solver: scheduling, hardware verification, puzzles, package dependencies. Learn to encode a problem as CNF and you can use a whole family of tools. The source is split into mtl/ (a small template library), utils/, core/ (the core solver) and simp/ (an extended solver with simplification), so it is practical to read as well as run.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the solver's options, including the heuristics and restart settings you can tune.
Runs the solver on a CNF file and reports whether it is satisfiable, with a model if so.
Runs with flags that, per the README, reproduce the heuristics of version 2.0.

entry.whats_unique: It is a compact, readable solver that still won industrial categories at SAT 2005, which made it a standard base for teaching and for building other tools on top of.
entry.caveats: The README has unfinished TODO sections, shows no release dates, and does not explain the solving algorithm, so you will need a CNF file of your own and outside reading.
